Dangote Petroleum Refinery’s initial public offering (IPO) has recorded 172 per cent oversubscription, with N5.85 trillion in bids for 11.15 billion shares against 4.1 billion offered at N525 each.
Subscription data seen by Nairametrics showed the N5.85 trillion in bids far exceeded the company’s initial fundraising target of N2.15 trillion, underscoring massive investor appetite for the refinery and setting the stage for one of the most significant equity transactions in African capital market history.
The offering launched on September 14, 2026, initially offered approximately 4.1 billion ordinary shares at N525 each. The subscription period, initially scheduled to close on October 13, was subsequently extended to October 27 following regulatory approval.
The scale of demand surprised even capital market analysts.For every share available, investors applied for nearly three shares, a level of oversubscription rarely seen in the Nigerian market.
However, the subscription figures represent investor applications rather than final allotments, with the amount ultimately raised dependent on the allocation process and regulatory approvals.
The strong subscription performance highlighted both the strategic importance of the refinery and the depth of liquidity now available in the Nigerian capital market, driven by domestic and international investors seeking exposure to a major energy infrastructure asset.
Retail investor participation was a major feature of the IPO, supported by an extensive distribution network involving banks, stockbrokers and digital investment platforms.
The latest figures showed nearly 3.8 million subscribers, representing approximately 84.39 per cent of all subscribers.
Despite the huge number of retail applicants, the bulk of the money came from a handful of large investors. Just three subscribers accounted for approximately 46.72 per cent of the total shares subscribed, representing applications worth about N2.73 trillion.
One investor applied for 771 million shares worth about N405 billion, or 6.92 per cent of total demand. Two groups of five investors each applied for 671.5 million shares worth N352.54 billion and 667.91 million shares worth N350.65 billion, respectively.
The IPO also attracted significant interest from international institutional investors. Bloomberg earlier reported that the offering received approximately $4.1 billion in applications, comprising about $1.9 billion from Nigerian investors and a further $2.1 billion from prospective international investors.
According to the report, South Africa’s Public Investment Corporation (PIC), which manages approximately $220 billion in pension assets, sought a substantial allocation. Nigerian pension fund managers were also reported to have expressed interest in acquiring shares in the refinery.
The reported international demand reflects the refinery’s strategic importance as a major energy infrastructure asset and its potential role in transforming Africa’s petroleum refining industry.
With subscription demand substantially exceeding the original offer size, attention is now expected to shift to the allotment process.
Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) allowed Dangote Refinery to absorb up to 30 per cent of additional oversubscription on top of its base offer.
The offering forms part of the refinery’s broader financing strategy as it pursues an ambitious expansion programme intended to increase processing capacity to approximately 1.4 million barrels per day.
The refinery’s recent financial performance has also provided investors with a basis for evaluating its growth prospects. For the nine months ended September 2026, the company reported revenue of $22.48 billion, representing a 144.47 per cent increase compared with the corresponding period of 2025.
Profit after tax rose to $4.73 billion, compared with a loss of approximately $117 million in the corresponding period of the previous year.
